newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metro net seen in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Metro net seen in line with expectations.

text.p: Conglomerate Metro Pacific Corp said on Thursday its net income in 1996 jumped 64 percent to 843.9 million pesos, a figure which analysts described as within expectations after extraordinaries were ruled out.
The rise in earnings was due to the strong performance of its telecommunication and real estate subsidiaries and one-time gains, the company said.
The company is also engaged in the sale and manufacture of pharmaceutical products, packaging and the banking business.
Sales in 1996 rose 4.2 percent to 4.922 billion from 4.723 billion pesos in 1995, Metro Pacific, a unit of Hong Kong's first Pacific co Ltd said in a statement.
The company said profit before other income in 1996 reached 523.2 million pesos, up 21.3 percent compared with 431.4 million pesos in 1995.

The other income in 1996 amounted to 262.2 million pesos versus 285.5 million pesos in 1995. The other income was due to Metro Pacific's sale of its holdings in the convertible bond of Smart Communications Inc, its telecommunications affiliate; and gains from the reduction of its interest in packaging concern, AR Packaging Corp (ARPC).
"We're happy with the earnings of Metro Pacific considering that some subsidiaries were bleeding," said Ben Hermoso, an analyst at Dharmala Securities.
He particularly referred to Steniel Manufacturing Corp, which posted a bigger loss of 245.6 million pesos against 105 million pesos in view of difficult market conditions.

Analysts said Metro Pacific could post a net profit of 745 million to one billion pesos this year on the back of strong contributions from Smart and land sales from its Fort Bonifacio property at the edge of the financial district of Makati.
A group led by Metro Pacific holds a 55 percent interest in Fort Bonifacio Development Corp (FBDC) that will develop 214 hectares near Makati.

"FBDC recorded a net income of over one billion pesos for 1996, and the signed contracts of sale will provide a strong base of recurring earnings in subsequent years," Metro Pacific said in the statement.
"I'm rather bullish on Smart," said Mejia, since it had been expanding rapidly in the cellular phone business.

"I think in the long-term this is an excellent company. It has two business franchises - Smart and Fort Bonifacio," said Jose salceda, director of SBC Warburg. "The cash flow is mounting in Fort Bonifacio."

Mejia, said, however Metro Pacific is now expensive, trading at 29 times forecast earnings per share of 28 centavos versus the 18 times multiple for index-linked stocks. Metro Pacific closed at 8.10 pesos on Thursday, up 5.2 percent from the previous close of 7.70 pesos.
